en: The Philippines has exactly 7,641 islands, which is 534 more than the previously believed count of 7,107.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Mount Pinatubo's 1991 eruption was the second-largest of the twentieth century, ejecting about 10 cubic kilometers of volcanic material.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the mountains to the sea.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 900 square kilometers.
The Philippines is part of the Coral Triangle, which contains 76 percent of all known coral species in the world.
The Philippine eagle's wingspan reaches up to 2 meters, which is wider than the average height of a ten-year-old child.
Baguio City receives over 4,000 millimeters of rain yearly, which is roughly four times the global average annual rainfall.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an 8.2-kilometer navigable waterway, making it one of the longest underground rivers in the world.
Palawan is the largest Philippine province, covering 14,649 square kilometers, which is bigger than the entire country of Jamaica.
The Philippines has about 7 million hectares of forest reserves, which covers roughly 23 percent of the country's total land area.
The 2.16-kilometer San Juanico Bridge is the longest in the Philippines, spanning a distance equal to about 20 football fields.
